task: N-Queens, GRAM's sets (8x8: 7,224 train / 1,240 test rows; 10x10: 108,234 / 18,466)
data: GRAM dataset/build_nqueens_dataset.py at gram-release f2e32b9, --n 8 --remove-counts 5 6 7 and --n 10 --remove-counts 7 8 9 (seed 42, test ratio 0.15, no augmentation); rows split by distinct input
model: n^2 binary cells; one free 2x2 table W_p per unordered cell pair (all pairs) and a free input cost B_i in R^2 per cell; given queens clamped; no attack lines, rows, columns, diagonals or queen count supplied
training: PL of the free cells of every training row at its labeled solution + lam L1 (proximal), zero start, full-batch SGD with momentum and cosine decay; deterministic (seeds set the search and each seed has its own timed fit); no solver, no differentiation through inference
metrics: GRAM's: acc_n1 = first chain's board valid; acc_majority20 = majority vote of 20 independent chains (ties to the lower mean energy) valid; cov20 = Cov@20 with GRAM's cap of 20 completions, mean over test rows; cov20_group_mean = the same per-row coverage averaged within groups of rows with equal completion count (capped at 20), then unweighted over the groups, as GRAM's evaluator prints it (most likely the Cov@20 of GRAM's table); accuracies over test rows (an input with s solutions counts s times). first_stop_valid = the first chain stopped (test passed) on a valid board holding the givens (rule checker, not label match).
flop: per test row, mean over rows: flop_n1 one chain; flop_n20 all 20 chains; per chain 2c^2 + 2c + 1 to initialize and 5c + 14 per move (cram_nqueens.move_flop); RNG, comparisons, indexing not counted
timing: cold: the first fit in a fresh process (one per seed); warm: median of 7 further fits; from GRAM's token arrays in host memory to the inference-ready model (token conversion, transfer, reduction to distinct solutions, initialization, all updates, S, tau, delta and the temperature unit); CUDA context apart; GPU one H200; CPU one thread in a CPU-only job

recipe.chosen: NQ2/NQ3 rule: highest mean validation accuracy over seeds 0-2 (99.333%, 0 wrong stops, 14 cap failures, 2.33e5 flop); validation search used 1 chain, test uses 20 (chain 0 = N 1)

couplings_seed0.definition: J_ij = W[1,1] - W[1,0] - W[0,1] + W[0,0] (queen-queen interaction of the pair); h_i = E(only cell i holds a queen) - E(empty board); E = const + sum h_i x_i + sum J_ij x_i x_j

recipe.chosen: NQ2/NQ3 rule: highest mean validation accuracy over seeds 0-2 (73.777%, 6,611 wrong stops, 1,791 cap failures in 32,040 chains, 9.88e5 flop); validation search used 1 chain, test uses 20 (chain 0 = N 1)

training_methods.pilot: the free-table energy of cram/cram_nqueens.py trained by pl, mpl, mpf, dsm (10,000 updates) and cd, pcd, chl (2,000 updates), none differentiating through a solver; per method the validation choice of lr, knob, lam, alpha, stopping test and T; 3 seeds, test once, 20 chains; fit times on one H200 (cold, warm median of 7), CUDA context apart; Cov@20 as row mean (cov20) and GRAM's group mean (cov20_group_mean)

offset_energy.energy: n^2 binary cells (0 empty, 1 queen); a pair term that depends only on the two states and the offset (dr, dc) of the cells (dr = r_j - r_i >= 0, dc > 0 when dr = 0; 2n(n-1) offsets); one unary cost shared by every cell; given queens clamped. table: a free 2x2 table per offset and a free 2-vector unary; ising: J_d x_i x_j per offset and h x_i (no term on empty cells). Nothing says which offsets attack.
offset_energy.prior: matched to EBR: 2D RoPE attention without an absolute position embedding (pair interactions depend on relative position)
offset_energy.optimizer: full-batch SGD on all training rows, momentum 0.5, cosine decay from lr to 0, zero start, 4,000 updates, no L1; per-offset preconditioning: the gradient of offset d is divided by m_d / mean(m), m_d its number of cell pairs
offset_energy.inference: focused heat-bath search (cram/cram_nqueens.solve), cap 20,000 moves, 20 chains; stop and T chosen on validation
